source.title: Harnessing Synthetic Datasets: The Role of Shape Bias in Deep Neural Network Generalization
source.authors: Elior Benarous; Sotiris Anagnostidis; Luca Biggio; Thomas Hofmann

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Tests shape bias and downstream generalization for CNNs and ViTs pretrained on synthetic datasets, a new setting relative to the listed versions; it does not test the natural-label memorization/generalization claim directly.
record.gate_note: Reports shape-bias measurements and downstream Tiny ImageNet validation accuracy for models pretrained on synthetic datasets. The paper also reports cited findings and background claims, which are not study results and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether shape bias predicts transfer accuracy after synthetic-data pretraining, which is outside V1–V8. Its CNN–ViT comparisons do not test CNNs versus fully connected networks. Adam and batch size are held fixed; none of the other version-specific interventions or measures is evaluated.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that architecture, supervision, diversity and naturalism complicate using shape bias alone to predict generalization. They suggest shape bias as a proxy for sample diversity; this is a proposed interpretation rather than an independently validated diversity measure.
record.recipe_differences: Self-supervised pretraining on synthetic image datasets, K-NN shape-bias measurement, and downstream Tiny ImageNet fine-tuning and validation evaluation; differs from the listed versions' interventions and measurements of memorization/generalization gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture, supervision type, ViT patch count, synthetic dataset, and training-data fraction affect the measured shape bias or downstream accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Shape-bias trajectories depend on architecture and supervision. ResNets have greater shape bias than ViTs, and the two ViT patch configurations differ substantially.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: K-NN shape bias depends on architecture and supervision as well as training data.

fits_no_version.finding: StyleGAN-Random produces the highest aggregate shape bias, whereas Shaders-21k StyleGAN produces the best downstream Tiny ImageNet accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shape bias alone does not rank transfer accuracy across these synthetic pretraining datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Shape bias increases with Tiny ImageNet sample count but varies little with synthetic sample count; Fractals and StyleGAN-Sparse peak at 25% and 5%, respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sensitivity of shape bias to sample count differs across datasets and may provide evidence about shape diversity.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2023 Workshop on Synthetic Data Generation with Generative AI
record.problems: The main figures do not provide exact values in the supplied text; Figure 2 aggregates three architectures and reports bounds rather than all model-specific outcomes. Downstream evaluation is on Tiny ImageNet after only two epochs of supervised fine-tuning. No uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Figure 2 reports aggregate curves over three architectures; the text does not provide recoverable dataset-specific exact values, so rows record the stated textual comparisons and figure-only outcomes.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error and the interpolation threshold.
CNN versus fully connected test error, learned local connectivity, and initialization from trained CNNs.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD performance under limited or broader tuning and recovery interventions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epochs and recipe changes that reduce the penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error and interactions with dataset size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Memorization-based example selection, removal and retraining compared with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because their measures address a different claim. This does not negate the paper's reported shape-bias findings. Exact plotted values are unavailable in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization versus natural-label generalization is not measured.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
CNN versus fully connected image classification is not compared; the architectures compared are ResNets and ViTs.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization is not compared.
Large versus small batch sizes and generalization gaps are not compared.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and training-test gaps are not measured.
Memorized training examples are not identified or removed.
